I've farmed these 10.1 mu for 25 years, since I was 19. My old man taught me the basics, and I've picked up things from village trainings and talking to the input dealer in town. I grow wheat after maize and maize after wheat, same as everyone in Quzhou. I've got seven people at home, but my wife and eldest son work in a factory in Handan, so we have some cash coming in. That lets me buy what I need, but I still count every yuan. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost.

**Wheat:** I sow in early October. I use improved seed — about 25 jin per mu. I buy the same variety my neighbor Lao Zhang switched to three years ago. His yield went up and his wheat didn't lodge, so I changed too. For fertilizer, I spread two 50-jin bags of compound fertilizer per mu when I sow. Then I topdress with urea twice — once when the wheat turns green, and again at jointing — about 40 jin of urea total per mu. I know that is a lot, but I'd rather put too much than too little. I irrigate three times with my well: the overwinter water, at jointing, and at heading. The electricity costs me, but three times is what this wheat needs. I spray herbicide right after sowing, and once in April for aphids or rust. I hire the rotary tiller before planting.

**Maize:** Right after I cut wheat in early June, I rotary till and plant hybrid maize. I sow about 4 to 5 jin per mu. I put down one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu — about 80 jin — at sowing, then topdress one 50-jin bag of urea per mu at big trumpet stage. I irrigate twice: once if the sowing is dry, and once at big trumpet. If July is really wet I might skip one, but two times is safe. I spray herbicide at seeding and insecticide once for corn borer. 

I don't mess with what works. Last year I got about 530 jin of wheat and 620 jin of maize per mu. This year I expect 550 jin wheat and 650 jin maize if the weather is normal. I watch what the bigger farms around me do. If they try something and it works, I do it the next year. If it fails, I laugh and stick to my own way.
